Synopsis:
 Released on October 19, 1993, Pearl Jam’s sophomore album Vs. arrived under an overwhelming crush of hype and commercial expectation. Having become global megastars off the back of Ten, the band retreated from arena-ready gloss and massive music video production to build something leaner, fiercer, and far more confrontationally raw. Reaming out the heavy reverb of their debut, producer Brendan O'Brien helped capture the group’s live aggression. Joined by new drummer Dave Abbruzzese—whose punchy, driving attack anchored the rhythm section alongside Jeff Ament—Pearl Jam channeled their frustration with fame, corporate music culture, and social injustice directly into the tape.
